overall: The AG found the Trust violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to post notice of its September 20, 2016 meeting, but accepted the November 17 re-discussion and re-vote as sufficient remedy and ordered no further action.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Trust failed to post notice of its September 20, 2016 meeting, at which it voted to appropriate funds for a project.
allegations.key_passage: While the Trust's failure to post notice of its September 20, 2016 meeting violated the requirements of the Open Meeting Law, see G.L. c. 30A, § 20(b), we find that the Trust took sufficient remedial action to address this violation by conducting the discussion again during a properly noticed meeting held on November 17, 2016.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Trust never created or posted minutes of its September 20, 2016 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: It appears, however, that the Trust did create meeting minutes, because those minutes were provided to us.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint; AG noted both notices listed the matter only as 'Cherry Street' and reminded the Trust of the specificity requirement.
allegations.key_passage: We take this opportunity to remind the Trust that meeting notices must contain sufficient specificity to reasonably advise the public of the issues to be discussed at the meeting.

remedy: No further action ordered; the Trust's re-discussion and re-vote at the properly noticed November 17, 2016 meeting was accepted as remedial action.
remedy_passage: we also find that the Trust took appropriate remedial action in response to this violation and order no further action.
